html:
SMTO-SKL-0132 — SMTO couldn't get an answer from Slack

GUID: fac6de37-03d2-55b0-bfd9-3b5655dae5b0
Slug: slack-provider-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO's request to Slack timed out, or Slack reported a temporary problem. This is usually a Slack outage or a network problem, not your settings.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Slack in your browser or app and make sure it loads and works normally. If Slack itself is having problems, SMTO can't reach it either.
  2. Check that the computer running SMTO is connected to the internet. SMTO talks to Slack from that computer, so a network problem there causes this error.
  3. If you asked SMTO to post, edit or delete something, check in Slack whether it already happened. SMTO never repeats a change on its own, so checking avoids doing it twice.
  4. Once Slack is working, ask the Agent for your request again. Reading from Slack is safe to repeat once Slack responds.

What success looks like

  • The Agent gets results from Slack.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a post or delete until you've checked Slack.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack Web API request hit the 180-second invocation deadline, used up its read retries after network or 5xx failures, or returned a non-success HTTP status classified as unavailable.

What this means

  • Slack reaches the client deadline, exhausts read retries for transport/server failures, or returns an unsuccessful status classified as unavailable. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack reaches the client deadline, exhausts read retries for transport/server failures, or returns an unsuccessful status classified as unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect status, deadline and safe transport detail rather than assuming a global outage.

How to fix it

  • Check network access from the Server host to slack.com and Slack's service status, then repeat the read. A write whose sending is uncertain is reported separately as slack.mutation_outcome_unknown and must be checked in Slack, not replayed.
  • Retry a bounded read after Slack recovers. Inspect provider state before issuing another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A later bounded read succeeds; prior mutation uncertainty is reconciled separately.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
